item.title: Koyasan Shukubo: Staying Overnight in a Temple — Guide
item.description: A shukubo stay is the heart of a Koyasan visit: around 50 of the mountain’s temples open their guest wings to travellers, giving visitors a night inside a working monastery. Rooms are simple tatami spaces with futon bedding and sliding screens, often looking onto a beautiful garden; dinner and breakfast are shojin ryori, the refined Buddhist vegetarian cuisine of tofu, mountain vegetables and Koya-dofu served on lacquer trays. Guests are welcome to join the monks for morning prayers at dawn and sometimes a fire ritual, and simply to experience the deep quiet of the mountain once the day visitors have gone.

item.title: Kyoto Yudofu Guide: The Art of Hot Tofu Cuisine
item.description: It sounds almost too simple to be a delicacy: blocks of tofu gently simmered in a clay pot of hot kombu broth, lifted out and dipped in soy sauce with a few condiments. Yet yudofu is one of Kyoto’s most beloved and refined dishes — a quiet celebration of the city’s exceptional tofu, born in the kitchens of its Zen temples. Eaten in a tatami room overlooking a garden, especially on a cold day, a yudofu meal is the essence of Kyoto: understated, seasonal, and built entirely on the quality of one humble ingredient.
